> unauthorized phone home

... is the case when the application or library you use sends a ping "home" to servers owned by the attacker/producer of the software.
Maybe it's called "phone home" because of ET, the movie? I'm not sure.

I thought about the difference between "phone home" and "data collection" and came to two example:

Some bulletin software used to "phone home" when you installed it because the developers wanted to know about new servers running their software. A simple anti-piracy feature. For sure, pirates immediately started to remove the "phone home" part of the software.
This is not "data collection" because there was no data involved. It was just a simple "ping" that enabled the bulletin developers to know about a new installation.
In this case "phone home" is a feature and a fair try to reduce piracy.

But bad actors can make use of this too: They could leave a backdoor (or "bugdoor") in a library and make use of the "phone home" part to know about new vulnerable servers/applications. Could be left in an "update" feature. Bugdoor + "phone home" update feature is a pretty stealthy combination for an attacker.

I hope I could help you with my explanation.
